summary: 1939 41-foot steel fire tower on the Appalachian Trail in the White Mountain National Forest; closed in 2014, restored and reopened in 2016; unstaffed since.

facts.design: 41-foot steel tower with a 7 by 7 foot cab, built from an International Derrick kit

access.note: Closed in 2014; reopened by the Forest Service after 2016 repairs. A 2020 Valley News photo caption says it is open to anyone willing to climb its steps. No 2025-26 notice found.

visit.trail_note: About four miles of Appalachian Trail from the Lyme-Dorchester Road trailhead, up the Lambert Ridge Trail.

events.note: First lookout on the summit, established by the New Hampshire Forestry Commission
Lookout temporarily discontinued except for emergency use
Current 41-foot steel tower. The register credits the NH Forestry Commission; Willhite says the CCC built it with Forest Service funds after the 1938 hurricane
Out of service; Dartmouth Outing Club leased it from the state for one dollar a year and staffed it during high fire danger
Station reopened by act of the NH Legislature; Willhite says staffed to 1980
Willhite gives 1973 as the last year of active service; the same page also says staffed to 1980
Site transferred to the NH Department of Public Works and Highways (Willhite)
Refurbished by the Dartmouth Outing Club with U.S. Forest Service funds
Registered January 19, 1996; nominated by Iris Baird, FFLA
Chapter visitor on August 30 found three of four guy cables not functional, a long-standing problem
The Forest announced in August 2014 that the tower was closed until critical repairs could be made
HistoriCorps replaced the roof and installed lightning protection in June 2016; the Forest Service reopened the tower to the public

notes_for_editor: Builder is disputed: the register credits the NH Forestry Commission, Willhite credits the CCC with Forest Service funds. Ownership is disputed: the register lists the U.S. Forest Service, Willhite says the site went to NH DPW&H in 1980, and the 2014 chapter report says the Forest acquired the tower in an AT land purchase (date not given). Willhite gives 1973 as last active year and also says staffed to 1980. The access line rests on a 2020 photo caption and a 2016 visit report; check current status before publishing. Record: the 1939 build event was missing and is added; height_m 12.5 matches the 41 ft in sources.
